answer: Onboarding throughput is allocated per invitation subtree rather than per account, so every subtree receives a fixed share of the network's new-identity capacity no matter how many keys it holds, and a farm's branches divide one allowance among themselves. Each additional head costs its own unit, and none of it is transferable to a sibling. Picture an ember holding one whisper of onboarding slots, divided among every plume below it: adding descendants divides the whisper again, so the farm's own plume count is what shrinks the whisper it already had.
